purpose: Daily candidate archive only; not formal knowledge-base admission
coverage: Bounded recent-conversation reference retrieval and independent first-party research across temporal robot action verification and video world-model diagnostics; not exhaustive.
source_handling: Only public literature links and categorical provenance; no private identifiers, raw conversations, personal details or mirrored PDFs.

chat_recovery.handling: GR-LIO already handled separately; no repeated daily recommendation. Other recovered assistant citations are not treated as user selections.

records.title: Looking Back to Move Forward: Temporal Verification for Generative Robot Policies
records.reading_boundary: Abstract record, methods 4.1–4.3, experiments 5, ablations, implementation and latency Appendix B, official project page. No independent reproduction or code execution.
records.license: CC-BY-4.0 as shown on arXiv HTML; no source material mirrored
records.baseline_change: Frozen pi0.5 plus learned history-conditioned candidate ranking and optional generation-time guidance.
records.claim_status: Experimental numbers are author-reported. Prioritizing verification-only under tight latency is an inference from their ablation, not a guaranteed deployment result.
key_limits: Learned compatibility is not a formal safety guarantee.
Verifier requires training; no extra expert demonstrations does not mean training-free.
Real-world completion scores are not binary success rates.

records.title: Tracking Is Not Permanence: What Video World Models Keep of a Hidden Object
records.reading_boundary: Methods 3–3.5, results 4–4.6, Table 1, limitations 5 and Appendix J, benchmark protocol and Table 10. No independent reproduction.
records.license: arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license as shown on HTML; no source material mirrored
records.baseline_change: Paired hidden-object state readouts separate encoder information from predictor retention, beyond whole-video physics scores.
records.claim_status: Readout and curriculum findings are author-reported on specified checkpoints. Using matched occlusion controls for robot world-model evaluation is a research suggestion.
key_limits: Main tests use synthetic scenes; readout thresholds do not establish zero residual information.
Mask geometry and scoring protocol affect conclusions.
Training and test share a renderer; no IntPhys 2 improvement.
